```{=html}
    <g id="convtab-bars"></g>
  </svg>

  <div class="convtab-info" id="convtab-info">Each cell is P(X=j)P(Y=k) &mdash; the product, because X and Y are independent.</div>
</div>

<style>
.convtab-wrap { width: 100%; }
.convtab-btnrow { display: flex; gap: 8px; justify-content: center; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-bottom: 6px; }
.convtab-btn {
  font-size: 0.8em; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px;
  border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; background: #f1f5f9; color: #1e293b;
  cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s;
}
.convtab-btn:hover { background: #e2e8f0; }
.convtab-btn.active { background: #1e293b; color: #ffffff; border-color: #1e293b; }
.convtab-rst { background: #ffffff; border-color: #94a3b8; }
.convtab-svg { width: 100%; height: auto; max-height: 430px; display: block; margin: 0 auto; }
.convtab-lab { font-size: 15px; fill: #1e293b; font-weight: 600; }
.convtab-hdr { font-size: 15px; fill: #475569; font-weight: 600; }
.convtab-small { font-size: 12px; fill: #64748b; }
.convtab-cell { transition: fill 0.3s ease; }
.convtab-cellnum { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; transition: fill 0.3s ease; }
.convtab-info { text-align: center; margin-top: 6px; font-size: 0.82em; font-family: 'Courier New', monospace; color: #1e293b; }
</style>

<script>
(function() {
  const NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
  const pX = [1, 3, 3, 1];
  const pY = [1, 2, 1];
  const TX = 90, TY = 118, CW = 78, CH = 58;
  const BX = 470, BBASE = 380, BTOP = 120, MAXP = 12;
  const found = {};

  function cellId(j, k) { return 'convtab-c-' + j + '-' + k; }

  function build() {
    const g = document.getElementById('convtab-cells');
    if (!g) return;
    for (let j = 0; j <= 3; j++) for (let k = 0; k <= 2; k++) {
      const x = TX + k * CW, y = TY + j * CH;
      const r = document.createElementNS(NS, 'rect');
      r.setAttribute('id', cellId(j, k));
      r.setAttribute('x', x); r.setAttribute('y', y);
      r.setAttribute('width', CW - 3); r.setAttribute('height', CH - 3);
      r.setAttribute('fill', '#e2e8f0');
      r.setAttribute('stroke', '#94a3b8');
      r.setAttribute('rx', 3);
      r.setAttribute('class', 'convtab-cell');
      g.appendChild(r);
      const t = document.createElementNS(NS, 'text');
      t.setAttribute('id', cellId(j, k) + '-t');
      t.setAttribute('x', x + (CW - 3) / 2); t.setAttribute('y', y + 35);
      t.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
      t.setAttribute('fill', '#475569');
      t.setAttribute('class', 'convtab-cellnum');
      t.textContent = (pX[j] * pY[k]) + '/32';
      g.appendChild(t);
    }
  }

  function drawBars() {
    const g = document.getElementById('convtab-bars');
    if (!g) return;
    g.innerHTML = '';
    for (let t = 0; t <= 5; t++) {
      const cx = BX + t * 70;
      const lb = document.createElementNS(NS, 'text');
      lb.setAttribute('x', cx); lb.setAttribute('y', BBASE + 20);
      lb.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
      lb.setAttribute('class', 'convtab-small');
      lb.textContent = t;
      g.appendChild(lb);
      if (found[t] === undefined) continue;
      const h = (found[t] / MAXP) * (BBASE - BTOP);
      const r = document.createElementNS(NS, 'rect');
      r.setAttribute('x', cx - 20); r.setAttribute('y', BBASE - h);
      r.setAttribute('width', 40); r.setAttribute('height', h);
      r.setAttribute('fill', '#2563eb'); r.setAttribute('rx', 3);
      g.appendChild(r);
      const n = document.createElementNS(NS, 'text');
      n.setAttribute('x', cx); n.setAttribute('y', BBASE - h - 8);
      n.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
      n.setAttribute('class', 'convtab-small');
      n.textContent = found[t] + '/32';
      g.appendChild(n);
    }
  }

  function show(t) {
    const terms = [], cells = [];
    let total = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j <= 3; j++) {
      const k = t - j;
      if (k >= 0 && k <= 2) {
        total += pX[j] * pY[k];
        terms.push('(' + pX[j] + '/8)(' + pY[k] + '/4)');
        cells.push(cellId(j, k));
      }
    }
    for (let j = 0; j <= 3; j++) for (let k = 0; k <= 2; k++) {
      const on = cells.indexOf(cellId(j, k)) >= 0;
      const r = document.getElementById(cellId(j, k));
      const tx = document.getElementById(cellId(j, k) + '-t');
      if (r) r.setAttribute('fill', on ? '#2563eb' : '#e2e8f0');
      if (tx) tx.setAttribute('fill', on ? '#ffffff' : '#475569');
    }
    found[t] = total;
    drawBars();
    const info = document.getElementById('convtab-info');
    if (info) info.innerHTML = 'P(T = ' + t + ') = ' + terms.join(' + ') + ' = ' + total + '/32';
  }

  function reset() {
    for (let t = 0; t <= 5; t++) delete found[t];
    for (let j = 0; j <= 3; j++) for (let k = 0; k <= 2; k++) {
      const r = document.getElementById(cellId(j, k));
      const tx = document.getElementById(cellId(j, k) + '-t');
      if (r) r.setAttribute('fill', '#e2e8f0');
      if (tx) tx.setAttribute('fill', '#475569');
    }
    document.querySelectorAll('.convtab-btn').forEach(function(o) { o.classList.remove('active'); });
    drawBars();
    const info = document.getElementById('convtab-info');
    if (info) info.innerHTML = 'Each cell is P(X=j)P(Y=k) &mdash; the product, because X and Y are independent.';
  }

  build();
  drawBars();
  document.querySelectorAll('.convtab-btn').forEach(function(b) {
    if (b.id === 'convtab-reset') return;
    b.addEventListener('click', function() {
      document.querySelectorAll('.convtab-btn').forEach(function(o) { o.classList.remove('active'); });
      b.classList.add('active');
      show(Number(b.dataset.t));
    });
  });
  const rb = document.getElementById('convtab-reset');
  if (rb) rb.addEventListener('click', reset);
})();
</script>
```

## What Did We Just Build?

::: {.fragment}
Collecting the six answers:

$$\frac{1}{32},\; \frac{5}{32},\; \frac{10}{32},\; \frac{10}{32},\; \frac{5}{32},\; \frac{1}{32}$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
Those numerators are $\binom{5}{0}, \binom{5}{1}, \dots, \binom{5}{5}$ — so

$$T = X + Y \sim \text{Bin}\!\left(5, \tfrac12\right)$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-important title="Not a coincidence"}
$\text{Bin}(3,\tfrac12) + \text{Bin}(2,\tfrac12) = \text{Bin}(5,\tfrac12)$ when the two are independent.
:::
:::

## Theorem: Sum of Independent Binomials

::: {.callout-note title="Theorem"}
If $X \sim \text{Bin}(n, p)$, $Y \sim \text{Bin}(m, p)$, and $X$ is **independent** of $Y$, then

$$X + Y \sim \text{Bin}(n+m,\, p)$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-warning title="Two conditions, both essential"}
- the **same** success probability $p$
- **independence** of $X$ and $Y$
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
We give two proofs — the first is one line, the second is the algebra.
:::

## Proof 1: A Story Proof {.smaller}

**Setting.** ECON211 has two sections: $n$ students in section A, $m$ in section B. Each student independently attends today's lecture with probability $p$.

::: {.incremental}
- $X$ = attendees from section A $\sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$
- $Y$ = attendees from section B $\sim \text{Bin}(m,p)$
- Sections are separate groups of students, so $X$ and $Y$ are independent
:::

::: {.fragment}
Now look at $X + Y$: it is the **total number of attendees** among $n + m$ students, each attending independently with probability $p$.
:::

::: {.fragment}
That is exactly the Binomial story with $n+m$ trials. Hence $X+Y \sim \text{Bin}(n+m, p)$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-important title="Why story proofs are worth learning"}
No algebra at all. We recognized the *generative process* instead of manipulating formulas.
:::
:::

## Proof 2: Convolution + Vandermonde {.smaller}

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
Write $q = 1-p$ and condition on $X$ (this is the LOTP):

::: {.fragment}
$$P(X+Y = k) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} P(X+Y = k \mid X = j)\,P(X=j) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} P(Y = k-j)\,P(X=j)$$

using independence to drop the conditioning.
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$= \sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{m}{k-j} p^{\,k-j} q^{\,m-k+j} \binom{n}{j} p^{\,j} q^{\,n-j} = p^k q^{\,n+m-k}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{m}{k-j}\binom{n}{j}$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
The sum is **Vandermonde's identity** — the same one we used to show the Hypergeometric PMF sums to $1$:

$$\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{n}{j}\binom{m}{k-j} = \binom{n+m}{k}$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$\Longrightarrow \quad P(X+Y=k) = \binom{n+m}{k} p^k q^{\,n+m-k} \qquad \blacksquare$$
:::
:::

## Warning: $X + Y$ is Not $2X$ {.smaller}

::: {.callout-warning title="A tempting shortcut that is wrong"}
If $X \sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$ and $Y \sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$, is $X + Y = 2X$?
:::

::: {.fragment}
**No.** $X + Y$ requires two **separate** r.v.s. Adding $X$ to itself gives $2X$, a completely different random variable.
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**$X + Y$, independent**

$\sim \text{Bin}(2n, p)$

support $\{0,1,2,\dots,2n\}$
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**$2X$**

not Binomial

support $\{0,2,4,\dots,2n\}$ — always even
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
Both have the same "average size", but $2X$ can never take an odd value. Same distribution for $X$ and $Y$ does **not** mean $X$ and $Y$ are the same r.v.
:::

## The Binomial, Rebuilt from Bernoullis

::: {.callout-note title="Theorem"}
If $X \sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$, then we can write

$$X = X_1 + X_2 + \dots + X_n$$

where $X_1, \dots, X_n$ are i.i.d. $\text{Bern}(p)$.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Proof.** Let $X_i = 1$ if trial $i$ is a success and $0$ otherwise. Imagine one person assigned to each trial, raising a hand if their trial succeeded. Counting raised hands is the same as adding the $X_i$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-important title="Why this matters"}
We have turned a distribution into a **sum of simple pieces**. This decomposition is the single most useful trick in the rest of the course — it is how we will compute expectations and variances almost effortlessly.
:::
:::

## Your Turn {.smaller}

::: {.callout-caution title="Question 4"}
A delivery service has two couriers. Today Aigerim has $10$ deliveries and Nurlan has $15$; each delivery is completed on time independently with probability $0.8$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be their numbers of on-time deliveries.

(a) Name the distribution of $X + Y$.

(b) A student writes "$X + Y \sim \text{Bin}(25, 1.6)$". What went wrong?

(c) Tomorrow Aigerim has the same $10$ deliveries again. Is her two-day total $\text{Bin}(20, 0.8)$?

(d) Is $2X$ $\;\text{Bin}(20, 0.8)$?
:::

::: {.fragment}
(a) $X + Y \sim \text{Bin}(25, 0.8)$.
:::

::: {.fragment}
(b) The parameters are not both added — $n$ adds, $p$ stays. And $p = 1.6$ is not a probability: a category error.
:::

::: {.fragment}
(c) Yes, **if** the two days are independent with the same $p$. That is a modelling assumption, not a fact.
:::

::: {.fragment}
(d) No. $2X$ is even with probability $1$.
:::

## Summary {.smaller}

::: {.callout-important title="One random variable"}
$g(X)$ is an r.v.: apply $X$, then apply $g$. To get its PMF:
**group** the $x$'s sharing the same $g(x)$, then **add** their probabilities.
$$P(g(X)=y) = \sum_{x:\,g(x)=y} P(X=x)$$
One-to-one $g$: probabilities are just **relabelled**.
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-important title="Several random variables"}
$g(X,Y)$ is an r.v. on the common sample space. Same recipe: group the outcomes giving the same value, add.
For sums with $X \perp Y$: $\;P(X+Y=t) = \sum_x P(X=x)P(Y=t-x)$.
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-warning title="Three traps"}
1. Multiplying a PMF instead of moving it sideways
2. Forgetting to merge mass when $g$ is not one-to-one
3. Treating $X+Y$ (two r.v.s) as $2X$ (one r.v.)
:::
:::
